analysis:
Examined both inference documentation excerpts, file metadata, the SDK gitlink update and all supplied Events bridge hunks against the canonical index and detailed T-041. EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift:15,32,64 adds and forwards an optional request stop-string scope; :159-160 passes it to matchedStopSequence when recording usage after stop/length completion. This appears to align reporting with request-specific stop matching rather than introducing an authorization or output-disclosure control. No supplied hunk changes encryption, serving grants, cache salts, SSD persistence, reservation release or payment accounting, and no concrete regression is established.
The documentation change at inference.md:2126 describes excluding reasoning and parsed tool-call spans while retaining whole-output matching for native block execution. The supplied :4923-5433 excerpts are unchanged per the complete range map; their cluster media lifetime, tenant-partition, bilateral retirement and qualification descriptions are context, not new controls or proof of implementation.
Material coverage limits remain: libs/mlx-swift-lm:1 advances the dependency revision without its implementation diff. Integration must review that revision's stop matcher/parser changes and verify request scope propagation through submission, actual StopHoldback enforcement and EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift replay, including prompt-open reasoning, parsed versus literal tool tags, streaming boundaries and native block requests. Confirm reporting does not attribute hidden-span matches or diverge from actual termination. Inspect dependency effects on cancellation and cache ownership/isolation (T-010, T-028, T-041), and plaintext output handling (A-001/T-008). The default nil scope alone does not prove callers omit the required scope. These unresolved contracts require further source review, not a vulnerability finding.
